page: Amazon Web Services r6i.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It features the x86_64 architecture powered by 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processors, providing 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The server is configured with 1024 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, delivering 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached storage options, and no discrete GPUs are present. Network baseline bandwidth provides up to 50 Gbps of throughput.

In computational benchmarks, the hardware displays strong multi-core scaling alongside average single-thread throughput. Multi-core evaluations such as stress-ng and PassMark CPU place the instance in the upper quartiles, augmented by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic hardware acceleration. The memory subsystem demonstrates high read throughput at 334.71 GB/s for uncached transfers and 6620.52 GB/s for cached operations. In transactional evaluations, the platform demonstrates strong performance, recording 107.75 million Redis SET operations per second and 72.88 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

Resource tradeoffs reflect the specific configuration: single-core benchmark metrics and large-scale language model inference throughput remain in average to low tiers due to standard clock frequencies and the absence of hardware accelerators. Cost efficiency is optimized for scale-up architectures requiring extensive RAM allocations per CPU socket rather than high single-threaded performance or local high-speed scratch disks. The server is suited for memory-intensive production enterprise applications, in-memory key-value databases, distributed caching layers, and high-throughput data processing.

Equipped with 1024 GB of DDR4 system memory at 3 GHz, the platform provides an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration contains no discrete GPUs and relies on remote storage because no local storage is bundled, while network baseline connectivity reaches 50 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate upper-tier multi-threaded compute and encryption performance alongside strong memory bandwidth reaching 334.71 GB/s for uncached transfers and 107.75 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core speeds remain average, and large-scale model inference throughput is limited without dedicated accelerators. From an efficiency standpoint, the instance delivers high resource density for scale-up memory architectures. It is well matched for memory-intensive workloads including in-memory enterprise databases, extensive caching layers, and distributed analytics pipelines.
